column1: # SHARED hand-verified N64-anim -> 3DS-CSAB corrections, read by the charcompare tool
# (which also WRITES this file via "Save overrides") AND the Python generators
# (tools/gen_animmap_inc.py for the game table, tools/gen_charcompare_index.py for the
# tool index). These OVERRIDE animmap.json's auto-picked best for a (zar, n64anim) pair.
# Columns are tab-separated: zar <TAB> n64anim <TAB> csab. '#' lines and blanks are ignored.
# The original 4 hand-verified disagreements migrated from the formerly hand-maintained
# zelda3d_animmap.inc (verified in-game; the auto-picker chose differently):
# En_Ko Kokiri kids (BACKLOG #8): the km1/kw1 skeletons animate from the SHARED object_os_anime
# bank (gKokiri*Anim), now wired in via zelda3d_anim_export SHARED_ANIM_BANKS. The anims are mostly
# 2-frame static-pose holds, so frame-delta auto-matching is meaningless -> map each by SEMANTICS
# to the km1_* CSAB (romaji: suwari=sit, agura=cross-legged, hiji=elbow, nokezori=lean-back,
# grass, ishi=stone/lift, kususu=giggle, asekaki=sweat, ukiuki=cheerful-stand). km1 carries the
# full CSAB set and kw1 shares it, so one /actor/zelda_km1.zar key resolves for both bodies.
# Cucco Lady (En_Niw_Lady, BACKLOG #38): gCuccoLadySkel (object_ane) animates from the shared
# object_os_anime bank via 4 anims, wired in through zelda3d_anim_export SHARED_ANIM_BANKS (allowlist).
# 9F94/0718/A630 auto-match their zelda_ane CSAB exactly by frame count (onegai_c/Ane_hanasu/oro_oro);
# only 07D0 needs a semantic pin: it is the neutral idle/wait but a 2-frame stub, so frame-delta picks
# the wrong CSAB -> map it to Ane_matsu (matsu = wait/idle). The runtime resolver disambiguates these
# os_anime OTR paths (also seeded under km1) by the model's ZAR.
# #119: child Nabooru at Spirit Temple crawlspace was mapped to nabor_agura_wait (agura=cross-legged
# sitting) -> baggy pants folded into a blob. Correct = nabor_hiza_wait (hiza=knee, kneeling, 24f,
# matches the 24f N64 KneeingAtCrawlspace anim). Verified live: kneels at the crawlspace, legs intact.
# En_Tg dancing couple: shares zelda_mu.zar with En_Mu haggling townspeople, but the two
# actors use DIFFERENT N64 anims (En_Tg = gDancingCoupleAnim, En_Mu = object_mu_Anim_0003F4).
# gDancingCoupleAnim was auto-picked to mu_matsu (the townsperson wait clip) -> couple stood
# in the shopkeeper's idle pose instead of dancing. Correct = tg_matsu (dance clip, same ZAR).
